hip_flex.source: ACE Romanian Deadlift: push the hips back and lower the weight until tension is felt along the hamstrings, bar tracking to about the mid-shin; no exact angle is given, so 75 degrees is an illustrative end for that depth (thin source, flagged for an owner device check)

knee_flex.source: ACE Romanian Deadlift: "keep a slight bend in both knees" (no exact angle given); ThatFitFriend (Mistake 3, "Squatting Your Hinge"): the knee bend should stay small enough to keep "higher hips and less knee bend" through the hinge. 10 to 20 degrees is illustrative, inside the AAOS knee row

torso_lean.source: ACE Romanian Deadlift: keep a straight back; the trunk stays rigid on the pelvis through the hip hinge (the lean itself comes from hip_flex, not the spine)

muscles.peakSource: ACE Romanian Deadlift: the hips push back and the weight lowers "until feeling some tension along the back of the legs," so hamstring effort is highest at that stretched bottom, just before the drive back to standing

mistake.name: Squat the hinge

tells.text: The knees bend forward like a squat instead of holding their angle.
The hips barely go back, turning the hinge into a squat.

mistake.source: ThatFitFriend (Mistake 3, "Squatting Your Hinge"): "When we bend too much at the knees during RDLs, we shorten the hamstrings and change the axis of rotation"; the fix is to keep "higher hips and less knee bend" while hinging back — the same fault shows on both the knee and the hip

sources: Contact fact (bar over mid-foot / kept against the legs): ACE Romanian Deadlift — "keeping the bar very close to the body while standing"
